title: Period conjecture for three-parameter Subtraction Nim (Ward/Moriwaki)
disposition_reason: Hypothesis (bounded counterexample) refuted as worded: source defines 'period' non-minimally (Moriwaki arXiv:2606.11658 Definition 2), so r302's witness S=(1,3,5) (minimal period 2) does NOT contradict the conjecture since a+b=4 is a period (2|4). The literal divisibility form (minimal eventual period m divides one of a+b, b+c, c+a) is Ward's open conjecture (arXiv:1606.04029 Case II, computationally verified there for s3<=4096): no counterexample found in exact scans to c<=40 (9500 triples, zero violations) and no full-scope proof mechanism survived caps. The periodic-solution classification route is provably insufficient (bad unreachable solutions exist in scope), so any proof must control reachability from the true initial condition.

literal_source.primary: Ward, A conjecture about periods in subtraction games, arXiv:1606.04029v1 (2016), Conjecture 1 Case II: period p is a divisor of at least one of s_i+s_j (1<=i<j<=3) and equals the gcd of all such sums; Case I (s3=s1+s2) explicit closed form.
literal_source.restatement: Moriwaki, Subtraction Nim with Continuous Parameters, arXiv:2606.11658v1 (2026-06-10), Conjecture 1: 'The Nim value function of G(S) for S = {a, b, c} with 0 < a < b < c and c != a + b is periodic with a period a + b, b + c or c + a.' Definition 2: 'The minimality is not required for them.'
literal_source.mathdb_cached_record: campaigns/2026-10-25/twenty-proof-discrete-lane/sources/mathdb-375237.json sha256 c33184738c2da70900f5ffdd7dc11e0e984d0b3acff9987a61c9f4bf677dfbbd (1781 bytes); statement matches Moriwaki Conjecture 1 under Definition 2.
literal_source.secondary: Miklos-Post arXiv:2312.02426v1 (2023): 0/1 winning positions with seeds; own Conjecture 1 Per({a,b,c}) < 2c (no seed, verified c<=200); does not restate Ward's nim-value form.
literal_source.quantifiers: For all integers 0<a<b<c with c!=a+b: the nim sequence g(n)=mex{g(n-s): s in S, s<=n}, g(0)=0, is eventually periodic and some p in {a+b,b+c,c+a} is an eventual period; equivalently the minimal eventual period m divides one of a+b, b+c, c+a. No exceptions, no gcd/parity conditions, preperiod unrestricted (pure periodicity NOT claimed in general).
